briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for November 4, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis Warnings and Severe Impacts
sections.content: Prince William warned that the UK faces the terrible risk of more wildfires due to climate change, noting that the summer of 2026 was the first year he felt "concern" about the scale of wildfires [72, 99]. Domestically, significant climate variability is also evident, with temperatures reaching 30 degrees Celsius in October [8], and a nephrologist warned that climate change could lead to 710,000 heat-related deaths annually and threaten kidney health [2, 77]. According to a Lancet report, Bangladesh is projected to incur a revenue loss of 17.5 billion USD in 2025 due to climate change [97], and there is a projection that 2026 is likely to be recorded as one of the warmest years on record, alongside 2024 [106]. UK Climate Minister Katie White emphasized that COP31 must respond to 'truly terrifying' scientific facts, reminding us that climate change is having widespread impacts, including threatening food security and leading to the loss of wild olive habitats [83, 84, 91, 105].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Action Discussions and Limitations
sections.content: Brazil concluded the COP30 meeting by presenting a fossil fuel and forest roadmap, and ahead of COP31, urged discussions on a global fossil fuel phase-out, emphasizing a transition from discussion to action [78, 89, 95, 96, 103]. Students from Yale School of the Environment are expected to attend COP31 [79], and issues of climate vulnerability in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and measures to enhance climate security will be addressed as key agenda items at COP31 [86, 87]. However, a critical analysis has been raised, stating that even if all new climate targets set at COP31 are met, the reduction by 2035 will only be 6%, which is merely one-tenth of the reduction needed to achieve the 1.5°C target [6]. Al Gore stated, in relation to the 2026 midterm elections, that the crisis of democracy must be addressed to solve the climate crisis [85], and research has also shown that while the climate change agenda often takes a backseat in election campaigns, voters remain interested [74].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Efforts for Carbon Neutrality Implementation and Awareness Raising
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are underway to spread a culture of carbon neutrality in practice. Yangju City held a 'Carbon Neutrality Citizen Practice Day' to share environmental conservation achievements and encourage daily life practices [14, 18, 24], and Goesan County is promoting citizen participation through tumbler certification and carbon neutrality point registration events [17, 28, 29, 31, 36, 40]. The Incheon Institute proposed expanding public transportation use to achieve the 2045 carbon neutrality target [13, 30], and Incheon is promoting carbon neutrality through changes in citizen mobility, such as saving 3.1 billion KRW by improving bus driving habits [16]. Furthermore, the 'Chorok Gyerim Energy Transition Center,' a resident-led carbon neutrality hub, was opened in Dong-gu, Gwangju City, Jeollanam-do [15, 32], and the Cheonan Carbon Neutrality Support Center successfully concluded its 'Giving New Life to Discarded Clothes' performance sharing session for its lifestyle practice group [37]. Kooksoondang is participating in the 'Companion Forest Project,' carrying out forest environmental conservation and carbon neutrality practice activities [39], and research results have also been announced, indicating that converting approximately 13% of domestic meat demand to alternative foods could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 3.45 million tons [70].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Facing Challenges
sections.content: The domestic renewable energy transition is progressing rapidly, with the 100 GW target now entering the implementation planning phase, marked by events such as the 'Forum for Advanced Power Industry in the Era of 100 GW Renewable Energy' [43, 58, 61]. Korea Philip Morris's Yangsan plant achieved a significant milestone by converting to 100% renewable energy and receiving a ministerial commendation in the field of renewable energy industry development [44, 55, 57, 60, 62, 63]. Busan Port is pursuing the establishment of a wind-powered RE100 port, the Saemangeum region is expanding its renewable energy target to 10 GW, and Hyundai Motor Company plans to invest 1.3 trillion KRW in solar power [47, 51, 65, 68]. Pyeongchang County is actively pursuing a project to return renewable energy profits to its citizens and secure basic income funds through a 150 MW solar power generation agreement [49, 54, 56, 66]. However, it has been revealed that the renewable energy procurement rate for RE100 participating companies is only 12%, necessitating a complete overhaul of power plans [50], and warnings that renewable energy will not automatically expand despite the practical difficulties of using electric trucks in rural areas and the increase in AI data centers remain challenges that need to be addressed [34, 59].

briefing.closing: We hope today's briefing has helped deepen your understanding of climate change and encouraged practical action. This concludes the climate briefing for November 4, 2026.
